name: Eastman Chemical

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Eastman Chemical Company logo.svg)

description: Eastman is a specialty materials company that makes plastics, films, additives and fibers from a few core chemistries (polyester, cellulose and acetyl, alkylamines, and propylene), largely at its giant integrated Kingsport, Tennessee site and at Longview, Texas. Its largest businesses sell high-performance copolyesters (Tritan), windshield and window interlayers (Saflex) and window and paint-protection films (LLumar) to automakers and builders, and additives for coatings, crop protection, water treatment and personal care. A third segment sells commodity-like intermediates and plasticizers, and the Fibers segment sells acetate tow, mostly for cigarette filters, plus textile fibers. It also runs the world's largest polyester molecular recycling plant, which turns waste plastic into new resin sold under the Renew label. 2025 sales were $8.75 billion, net earnings attributable to Eastman $474 million, and about 55 percent of sales were outside the US and Canada.

gics.note: Per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 600 companies' (raw wikitext read 2026-10-27). Eastman was moved from the S&P 500 to the S&P SmallCap 600 on November 4, 2025 as 'more representative of the small cap market space' (same page). That list gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry are null.

hq.note: Headquarters and largest manufacturing facility (FY2025 10-K Item 1)

businessLines.name: Advanced Materials (AM)
businessLines.how: Materials sold by the pound or square meter to automakers, glass laminators, converters and, for films, through a dealer and installer network; priced on performance and application development rather than on raw material cost.
businessLines.description: Advanced interlayers (Saflex PVB sheet), performance films (LLumar and other window and paint-protection films) and specialty plastics (Tritan, Eastar and other copolyesters, cellulosic biopolymers).

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBIT (non-GAAP); FY2024 not read. About 31.4% of the $1,112M segment total before Other adjusted EBIT of $(182)M

businessLines.name: Additives & Functional Products (AFP)
businessLines.how: Small-volume additives sold into customers' formulations (paint, crop protection, water treatment, heat-transfer systems); each is a small part of the customer's cost, so customers stay with a qualified supplier and the business earns recurring repeat orders.
businessLines.description: Care additives (amine derivatives, organic acids), coatings additives (Texanol, Optifilm, solvents, polymers), functional amines, and specialty fluids (Therminol heat transfer, Skydrol aviation fluids).

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBIT (non-GAAP). About 46.4% of the $1,112M segment total, the largest share

businessLines.name: Chemical Intermediates (CI)
businessLines.how: Commodity-style chemicals sold by the pound at market-linked prices; mainly a low-cost feedstock supplier to Eastman's own specialty segments, with the excess sold to outside industrial customers.
businessLines.description: Oxo alcohols and derivatives, acetic acid and derivatives, ethylene, commodity solvents and plasticizers; sells the surplus of intermediates beyond what the specialty segments consume.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBIT (non-GAAP), a loss; about -3.4% of the segment total

businessLines.name: Fibers
businessLines.how: Sells acetate tow to cigarette makers under long-term variable-price arrangements, and supplies acetate flake to its China acetate tow joint venture (recognized as sales, with the venture's earnings in other income); textile yarn is a smaller growth effort.
businessLines.description: Acetate tow and triacetin (cigarette filters), Naia and Estron acetate yarn and staple fiber for apparel and home textiles, nonwovens, and acetate flake and acetyl raw materials sold to other acetate fiber makers.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBIT (non-GAAP). About 25.6% of the segment total; the highest margin of the four

brands.name: Tritan, Eastar, Spectar, Embrace, Eastman Aspira, Treva copolyesters and biopolymers
brands.share: Specialty plastics are 49% of AM sales (about $1.4B)

brands.name: Saflex (including Q Series acoustic and HUD interlayers)
brands.share: Advanced interlayers are 32% of AM sales (about $0.9B)

brands.name: LLumar, SunTek, V-KOOL, Gila, Flexvue (window and paint-protection films)
brands.share: Performance films are 19% of AM sales (about $0.5B)

brands.name: Texanol, Optifilm, EastaPure, Esmeri, Solus
brands.share: Coatings additives are 27% of AFP sales

brands.name: Therminol, Skydrol, SkyKleen, Marlotherm
brands.share: Specialty fluids and energy are 16% of AFP sales

brands.name: Estron acetate tow and Naia fiber
brands.share: Tow 69% and yarn/fiber 11% of Fibers sales

brands.name: Renew (molecular recycling), Aventa (compostable biopolymer)
brands.share: Not separately reported; the Kingsport recycling plant's output was about 2.5 times 2024 output
